metadata.title: About
metadata.description: Stichting Safe AI Netherlands develops the talent the Netherlands needs to address the risks of transformative AI. The talent pipeline, the foundation documents, and the people who run it.

mission.talent: Develop the talent the Netherlands needs.
mission.risks: Address the risks of transformative AI.
mission.contribution: Make a first real contribution possible.

hero.intro: That is the mission of Stichting Safe AI Netherlands. Transformative AI could reshape the economy, science, and society on the scale of a major historical revolution; whether that goes well is not decided yet. We are a national talent pipeline: local chapters on shared infrastructure, from first contact through courses and the Project Hub, with a handoff into the wider field. This page shows that path, what we have written down, and the people who run it.

path.heading: The Netherlands has the talent. It lacked the path.
path.trajectory: On the current trajectory, AI systems may soon do most economically and strategically important cognitive work, including AI research itself. The critical question is not only what AI will become, but whether enough people are ready to shape what happens next. Right now, far too few are working on that problem.
path.readiness: Nobody can name the exact timeline, and we will not pretend to. Readiness is not something the Netherlands has by default. It is something people build, while European institutions are staffing their AI safety functions in the next few years.
path.gap: The Netherlands has world-class universities, ASML at the centre of the global semiconductor supply chain, proximity to Brussels, and emerging AI safety groups. What it lacked was a unified civil-society voice and a clear path from interest to capability to meaningful contribution. SAIN was created to close that gap. We develop the people; the field puts them to work.

pipeline.heading: Anyone can start. The path narrows as you grow.
pipeline.whole: The Funnel Diagram is the whole organisation. The wide end is a free course anyone can join, no technical background required. The narrow end is full-time work on AI safety, in policy, research, industry or civil society. Between them sit the community, the Project Hub, and fellowships. Progress through it is visible, to us and to the person making it, and SAIN’s job is to make each next step reachable, so that every step someone takes compounds into a more effective mission.
pipeline.effort: We are open about where our effort goes. SAIN builds the wide end: getting people in, teaching foundations, and scaffolding a first real contribution such as a supervised research project. At the narrow end we mainly connect and refer, with introductions and referral letters.
pipeline.endings: We designed the pipeline with many good endings. Someone who takes one course and returns to law, medicine or public administration carries that knowledge into their profession, and a society fluent in AI risk is an outcome we actively want.
pipeline.soFar: So far the pipeline has produced more than 100 course graduates across nine-plus cohorts, currently around 60 a year, and peer-reviewed research at NeurIPS and ICLR. The aim for mid-2027 is 250 or more graduates a year, reached by running the same standardised course in more cities.

team.heading: A small leadership, close to the work.
team.intro: SAIN is led by its national director and the heads of growth, operations and projects. The leadership takes the strategic decisions; the chapters run the courses, events and communities.

documents.heading: The rules we hold ourselves to are public.
documents.intro: SAIN is a Dutch foundation, a stichting, the standard nonprofit legal form. The foundation holds the brand, the legal entity and the finances, so a local chapter never has to build those from scratch; chapters run their own courses, events and communities. Every programme is free. Three documents define how the whole thing works, and anyone can read them.
